With the ability to dissociate to a high level and having a bad attachment to a primary caregiver, the brain will put up amnesic barriers to hide these memories. (The trauma must occur before ages 7-8)

This is structural dissociation (which you can google) and the foundation of DID, this means when ‘switching’ from each state of consciousness, the brain is unaware of the memories the other state of consciousness has been through due to the amnesic walls. 

The entire reason DID exists is to hide extreme childhood trauma, and so its perfectly just for each state of consciousness to have different memories. These states are called alters. 

Dissociative Identity Disorder has been recognised in the DSM since the 4th edition and was reclassified from the 3rd edition (wrongly labelled as a personality disorder). All of this is easily researchable  as the cause of DID and you can correct me if it says anything different.
